paper.title_en: Baryon transport from light to strange quarks
paper.abstract_en: The baryon number of a baryon is conventionally assumed to be shared equally among the baryon’s three valence quarks. An alternative model instead assigns it to a Y-shaped configuration of nonperturbative gluons, called a baryon junction, linking the three quarks. Neither picture has been experimentally verified. Because quarks carry the electric charge while the junction does not, comparing the movement of baryon number to charge number provides a means to distinguish the two pictures. Using the STAR isobar dataset of <math altimg="si3.svg"><mrow><msubsup><mrow/><mn>44</mn><mn>96</mn></msubsup><mtext>Ru</mtext><msubsup><mo>+</mo><mn>44</mn><mn>96</mn></msubsup><mtext>Ru</mtext></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si4.svg"><mrow><msubsup><mrow/><mn>40</mn><mn>96</mn></msubsup><mtext>Zr</mtext><msubsup><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mn>96</mn></msubsup><mtext>Zr</mtext></mrow></math> collisions at <math altimg="si5.svg"><mrow><msqrt><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub></msqrt><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>200</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi></mrow><mi>e</mi><mi>V</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, the mid-rapidity ratio of net-baryon yield B to net-charge difference <math altimg="si6.svg"><mrow><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Δ</mi></mstyle><mi>Q</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>(</mo><mtext>Ru</mtext><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>(</mo><mtext>Zr</mtext><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> in central collisions is found to be roughly twice the value expected from the quark picture. In γ*+Au interactions, the net-proton yield decreases with rapidity too slowly to be described by the quark picture. The same behavior is observed in net-proton and net-hyperon yields in hadronic Au+Au collisions across a wide range of beam energies. Furthermore, the stopping behaviors of net-Λ, net-Ξ, and net-Ω are similar to each other, consistent with the transport of a flavor-blind gluonic junction. All these results favor the baryon junction over quarks as the carrier of baryon number. We can further study how the junction behaves dynamically in other types of collision systems and how it depends on kinematic variables. Current electron-proton experiments at CLAS12, the analysis of net-Λ data from H1/HERA, and future high-statistics electron-ion collider measurements will provide further clarification.
